title: Headless Telegram Web testing mode (QR login via agent-browser)
body:
## What
qa-cli does not exist. Live Telegram tests currently risk opening Telegram.app or sending junk like PING-339-LIVE-PROOF into real chats. We need a dedicated CLI that drives Telegram Web (https://web.telegram.org/a/) in headless Chromium via the agent-browser CLI, shows a QR for phone login, persists the session, and never launches the desktop app. Evidence of the current gap: GitHub returned 404 for https://github.com/alex-mextner/qa-cli before this repo was created, and no /Users/ultra/xp/qa-cli checkout existed. This is an unbuilt CLI, so there is no screenshot of a broken UI yet; the observable broken state is the missing command and the live-test path that can open Telegram.app or spam production chats.

## Why (motivation)
Alex 2026-09-08: live Telegram tests are OK but MUST be HEADLESS. QR login in qa-cli; do NOT open Telegram.app; do NOT send junk into production chats as the default proof path.

## User impact
Agents and humans who need to exercise Telegram from a terminal can run qa telegram login, scan a QR with their phone, and re-run tests against a persisted headless Chromium session instead of the desktop Telegram.app. Default CI stays hermetic (fake/stub browser) and never touches real Telegram, so a PR cannot spam a real chat or pop a desktop app.

## Cost of inaction
Live Telegram tests keep launching Telegram.app or spamming real chats; there is no durable headless QR path, so every live proof either disturbs the human desktop or dumps junk like PING-339-LIVE-PROOF into production conversations.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `qa telegram login` exists, and when not logged in it saves a QR screenshot artifact and prints its path — proven by hermetic unit test with a fake browser (no network). — forced: CLI no UI; proven by named tests test_login_saves_qr_when_logged_out, test_agent_browser_argv_uses_agent_browser_not_telegram_app, test_status_logged_out_without_session
- [x] The login driver invokes `agent-browser` (never Playwright/Puppeteer wrappers, never `open -a Telegram`) and default pytest never hits live Telegram — proven by hermetic tests asserting argv and by live tests skipped unless QA_TELEGRAM_LIVE=1. — forced: CLI no UI; proven by named tests test_login_saves_qr_when_logged_out, test_agent_browser_argv_uses_agent_browser_not_telegram_app, test_status_logged_out_without_session
- [x] `qa telegram status` reports logged-in vs logged-out from the persisted session without launching Telegram.app — proven by hermetic unit test. — forced: CLI no UI; proven by named tests test_login_saves_qr_when_logged_out, test_agent_browser_argv_uses_agent_browser_not_telegram_app, test_status_logged_out_without_session

## Screenshots
(none)

## Links
- PR: https://github.com/alex-mextner/qa-cli/pull/4
- Merge commit: https://github.com/alex-mextner/qa-cli/commit/6e9423855037567fa7554c8e680613ef57b08088

## Skipped gates
- links: tokens such as Telegram.app, agent-browser, and PING-339-LIVE-PROOF are product names / banned proof strings, not GitHub issue or repo references
- screenshots: CLI with no app UI yet; the missing product has no screen to capture. Current evidence is the 404/absent checkout recorded in --what.

Shipped: merged via https://github.com/alex-mextner/qa-cli/pull/4.

title: Live-prove qa-cli Telegram Web QR via agent-browser
body:
## What
Run live proof of qa-cli Telegram Web against https://web.telegram.org/a/ using the product session qa-telegram. Confirm qa telegram status, then qa telegram login if logged-out, and capture a real painted QR at ~/.config/qa-cli/telegram-qr.png (or prove already logged-in). Login/status already shipped on main as qa 0.2.0 via https://github.com/alex-mextner/qa-cli/pull/2 and https://github.com/alex-mextner/qa-cli/pull/4. https://github.com/alex-mextner/qa-cli/issues/1 is closed. There is no send/read command; do not add one unless status is already logged-in. Never open Telegram.app and never message a production bot chat.

## Why (motivation)
The product claims QR login via agent-browser, but ~/.config/qa-cli does not exist and there is no live artifact proving Telegram Web actually paints a scannable QR. Unit tests cannot substitute for a live canvas on https://web.telegram.org/a/.

## User impact
Until a real painted QR (or a logged-in status) is captured, Alex cannot scan to complete the headless Telegram Web session, so qa-cli cannot be used to test Telegram Web at all.

## Cost of inaction
Shipped login/status stays unproven against live Telegram Web. A blank canvas or timeout-without-file would look fine in hermetic tests while the human still cannot scan and log in.

## Acceptance criteria

Proof: QR PNG plus pixel-stats file, or status stdout showing logged-in. — proof: ![proof](/Users/ultra/.config/qa-cli/telegram-qr.png)

title: Commit SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 in .ship-config
body:
## What
qa-cli origin/main has no repo-root .ship-config. After https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/624, env SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 is ignored; only a committed SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 line on the PR BASE branch disables gh ship's zero-GitHub-reviews gate (read from origin/<base>, never from the shipping PR's own HEAD). Evidence now: git show origin/main:.ship-config fails (path does not exist). Precedent: https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/commit/17431bf446dffd76016cf84704773a91806e93ba and merged https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/pull/451.

## Why (motivation)
Without a committed .ship-config on main, every qa-cli gh ship of a PR with no GitHub-side review is refused. The intended off-switch only takes effect after a normal merge to main. A machine-wide SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 export is ignored and must not be the standing policy.

## User impact
Agents and the maintainer cannot merge already-reviewed, CI-green qa-cli PRs. Work stays unshipped while merge is blocked on an empty GitHub reviews array, even when GitHub required_approving_review_count is already 0.

## Cost of inaction
Future qa-cli ships keep failing the ZERO GitHub reviews gate. Operators keep exporting SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 in the shell, which is ignored after https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/624, so ships stay stuck.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] origin/main contains a repo-root .ship-config whose only key is SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0. Proof: git show origin/main:.ship-config prints that line and nothing else. — proof: ![proof](/tmp/qa-cli-8-proofs/c1-git-show-ship-config.txt)
- [x] A PR exists adding only that one-line .ship-config and is shipped (or the exact remaining ship refusal is quoted). Proof: the PR URL plus merged state or quoted remaining refusal. — proof: ![proof](/tmp/qa-cli-8-proofs/c2-pr-merged.json)

## Screenshots

- PR: https://github.com/alex-mextner/qa-cli/pull/10
- Merge commit: https://github.com/alex-mextner/qa-cli/commit/d98e82643ce1d316d3957d07918ac467678e8144

## Skipped gates
- post-merge-acceptance: Criterion 1 is git show origin/main:.ship-config after this PR squash-merges to main; criterion 2 is the PR URL plus merged state. Neither is observable before the merge.
- screenshots: no UI; one-line committed ship-config ops off-switch, evidence is git show and gh pr view JSON

title: qa telegram login times out waiting for QR canvas even though QR renders successfully
body:
## What
`qa telegram login` reliably times out at its 60s QR-wait window against the real, live
https://web.telegram.org/a/ page — even though the QR code does render successfully. A
direct DOM probe taken immediately after each CLI timeout confirms the QR was already
painted. Reproduced 3/3 times.

Exact repro command:
```
cd /Users/ultra/xp/qa-cli && QA_TELEGRAM_LIVE=1 timeout 90 qa telegram login
```
Repeat 2-3x back-to-back against a logged-out live session (`QA_TELEGRAM_LIVE=1 qa telegram status` should report `logged-out` first).

Observed failure:
- Exit code: 1
- stderr:
  ```
  error: timed out waiting for Telegram Web QR canvas
  scan the QR with your phone and re-run: qa telegram login
  ```
- Wall time: ~60.3-60.7s each run (i.e. right at the `DEFAULT_QR_WAIT_TIMEOUT` boundary)
- Reproduced 3/3 consecutive times via the `qa` console-script + argparse dispatch (exactly
  `QA_TELEGRAM_LIVE=1 timeout 90 qa telegram login`), against a logged-out live session.
- Screenshots of the failure (QR code visibly rendered at time of CLI timeout):
  `/tmp/qa-live-login-timeout.png`, `/tmp/qa-live-login-timeout2.png`

Contradicting evidence — the QR *is* rendered. Immediately after each of the 3 CLI
timeouts, a direct JS DOM probe against that same live page returned proof the QR had
already painted:
```
agent-browser --session qa-telegram --restore qa-telegram eval "$(python3 -c 'from qa_cli.browser import _QR_VISIBLE_JS; print(_QR_VISIBLE_JS)')"
```
returned `"qr-visible"` every time — Telegram's real SVG QR code (inside `.qr-container`,
~280x280, with the Telegram paper-plane logo) was already on the page when the CLI gave up.
This confirms the QR-visibility detection heuristic itself is correct; the CLI just stopped
waiting before observing the state it was polling for.

Workaround that succeeded: a direct in-process call — bypassing the `qa` console-script and
the external `timeout` wrapper entirely:
```python
import qa_cli.telegram
qa_cli.telegram.login(...)
```
— succeeded in ~3s and saved a real, scannable QR code to
`~/.config/qa-cli/telegram-qr.png` (confirmed via screenshot).

Relevant code, `qa_cli/telegram.py:17`:
```python
DEFAULT_QR_WAIT_TIMEOUT = 60.0
```
(`DEFAULT_LOGIN_TIMEOUT = 300.0` is the line immediately above it, at line 16 — a prior
handoff note miscited the QR timeout constant as line 16; it is line 17 as of the current
file.)

Root cause — not conclusively isolated. Two live-only hypotheses, either or both may
contribute:
1. Telegram-side throttling: Telegram's live QR-issuance backend intermittently
   delays/throttles repeated QR requests from the same session in quick back-to-back
   succession during a single test run.
2. CLI/subprocess-wrapper overhead: a behavioral difference between invoking through the
   `qa` binary + external `timeout` wrapper vs. calling `qa_cli.telegram.login()`
   in-process (e.g. `subprocess` `capture_output` buffering under a wrapped process tree)
   adds enough latency/delay to blow through the 60s budget even though the underlying
   browser-side render itself is fast.

Suggested next step:
- Increase `DEFAULT_QR_WAIT_TIMEOUT` (`qa_cli/telegram.py:17`) to give more headroom, and/or
- Investigate why the CLI-wrapped path (`qa` binary + `timeout`) is slower/less reliable
  than the direct `qa_cli.telegram.login()` in-process call — e.g. instrument the poll loop
  with timestamps to see where the 60s budget is actually spent — with a live re-test to
  confirm whichever fix resolves the flake.

## Why (motivation)
`qa telegram login` reliably times out at its 60s QR-wait window against the real, live
https://web.telegram.org/a/ page even though the QR code does render successfully — a
direct DOM probe taken immediately after each CLI timeout confirms the QR was already
painted, and the QR-visibility detection heuristic itself is correct. Reproduced 3/3
times. Root cause is not conclusively isolated: it may be Telegram-side throttling of
repeated QR requests, and/or CLI/subprocess-wrapper overhead (the `qa` binary + external
`timeout` wrapper) adding enough latency to blow through the 60s budget even though the
underlying browser-side render itself is fast — a direct in-process call to
`qa_cli.telegram.login()` succeeded in ~3s where the wrapped CLI path timed out.

## User impact
`qa telegram login` — the CLI's primary QR-login entrypoint — is unreliable/flaky against
a real live Telegram Web session despite the underlying automation working correctly,
undermining trust in the tool's core login flow and forcing users to bypass the documented
CLI command in favor of calling internal Python functions directly.

## Cost of inaction
Users of `qa telegram login` — the CLI's primary QR-login entrypoint — keep hitting
unreliable timeouts against a real live Telegram Web session despite the underlying
automation working correctly, undermining trust in the tool's core login flow and forcing
users to keep bypassing the documented CLI command in favor of calling internal Python
functions (`qa_cli.telegram.login()`) directly.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Repro command above no longer exits 1 with the QR-canvas timeout error on 3/3 consecutive live runs against a logged-out session. — proof: ![proof](.proof/issue11/c1.txt)
- [x] If the fix is a timeout increase, the CLI still fails within a bounded time (not an indefinite hang) if the QR truly never renders. — proof: ![proof](.proof/issue11/c2.txt)

- creation: ![creation](/tmp/qa-live-login-timeout2.png)
- creation: ![creation](/Users/ultra/.config/qa-cli/telegram-qr.png)
- implementation: ![implementation](/tmp/qa-live-login-timeout.png)
